Method of Attack: Prototype Pollution via parseNested option allowing flattening of uploaded JSON data into nested objects, enabling denial-of-service (DoS) attacks and remote shell access
Remote code execution via reverse shell exploiting prototype pollution combined with templating engine EJS by overwriting outputFunctionName option to launch Node.js child_process
Impacted Systems: Node.js applications using express-fileupload with parseNested option enabled
Applications using EJS templating engine in conjunction with vulnerable express-fileupload
Attack Vector: Malicious HTTP requests with crafted Content-Disposition headers injecting __proto__.toString payloads
Indicators of Compromise: HTTP requests overriding Object.prototype.toString causing 500 errors
Payloads exploiting parseNested and EJS outputFunctionName option to spawn reverse shells
